links.outcome: Recognition of emergencies and appropriate escalation versus over-triage in simulated self-triage scenarios
links.effect: Both AI platforms correctly identified all 5 emergency cases; NHS 111 under-triaged one acute emergency. AI occasionally over-triaged non-emergencies (e.g., pyelonephritis sent to emergency assessment).
links.quote: Both AI platforms correctly identified all emergency cases; NHS 111 under-triaged one acute emergency.

links.outcome: Missed or delayed escalation of emergencies by conversational AI in simulated scenarios
links.effect: Both ChatGPT GPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Flash correctly identified all five emergency cases, while NHS 111 under-triaged one.
links.quote: Both AI platforms correctly identified all emergency cases; NHS 111 under-triaged one acute emergency.

screen.reason: The study empirically tests general-purpose LLMs (ChatGPT and Gemini) against NHS 111 on simulated patient vignettes for patient self-triage, but does not compare specific deployment practices or safeguards.
